page: Microsoft Azure E64d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores operating at a base speed of 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX-512 Foundation and Vector Neural Network Instructions), AES cryptography acceleration, and SHA extensions. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core density of 8.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a bundled 2458 GB local SSD.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations are also highly efficient, registering in the top tier at 298.57 GB/sec and 130.67 GB/sec respectively. The server demonstrates high throughput in database operations and key-value store workloads, achieving 62.33 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, single-core execution and large-model LLM text generation represent relative performance trade-offs, scoring in the average and weak tiers respectively.

Given its high memory density and integrated local SSD storage, the E64d_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that require rapid local scratch space without the overhead of external network storage. It is highly suited for relational database hosting, in-memory caching layers like Redis, large-scale software compilation, and data-intensive web serving.
